 Traveling through Portland International Airport this Thanksgiving? Here’s what to expect
 Published 4:00 am Friday, November 20, 2026
 By Hannah Seibold 
 Travelers at Portland International Airport wait to cross through security. 
 (Jonathan House/Portland Tribune) 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 If you’re flying through Portland International Airport this Thanksgiving, expect a busy holiday travel week.
 The airport is preparing for an estimated 383,000 travelers between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including arriving, departing, and connecting passengers.
 According to PDX, that would represent at least a 1% increase over roughly the same period last year.
 Sunday, Nov. 29, is expected to be the busiest day, with more than 63,000 passengers traveling through the airport. Monday, Nov. 30, is projected to follow closely behind, with approximately 59,000 travelers.
 Here’s what to know before heading to the airport.
 When to expect the biggest crowds
 Travelers flying home for Thanksgiving or returning after the holiday should plan for heavier airport traffic, particularly on Sunday and Monday.
 PDX recommends arriving at least two hours before departure to allow enough time for parking, curbside drop-off, airline check-in, and security screening.
 Travelers should also make sure they have the proper identification before arriving. A REAL ID-compliant driver’s license or another acceptable form of identification, such as a passport, is required for domestic air travel.
 Holiday markets and festive airport activities
 Those with extra time before their flights can enjoy a little holiday entertainment. PDX’s annual Holiday Markets return Nov. 23 through Dec. 21, with pop-ups in different concourses.
 The markets will feature local shop favorites, live music and visits from therapy animals throughout the holiday season.
 For those picking up friends or family, PDX is also bringing back its holiday parking promotion. From Nov. 15 through Dec. 31, visitors who spend $20 at participating pre-security shops and restaurants can receive two hours of complimentary parking.
 Tips for navigating PDX
 The airport’s main terminal project is now complete, but there are still a few helpful tools travelers should know about before making their way through the airport.
 Check security wait times: PDX tracks estimated TSA wait times on FlyPDX.com , allowing travelers to get an idea of what to expect at security.
 Use the airport map: The interactive map on FlyPDX.com helps travelers locate shops, restaurants, and airport amenities. It can also estimate walking times between destinations and identify accessible routes.
 Find your parking spot: If you’ve forgotten where you parked, PDX’s “Remember Where You Parked” tool provides step-by-step directions back to vehicles in the long- and short-term parking garages.
 Know where to explore: Travelers with time to spare can visit the Sensory Room in Concourse D or catch a short film at the Hollywood Theatre in Concourse C.
 What to know about baggage claim
 Travelers arriving at PDX may notice some updates to the baggage claim area. The airport is currently in the middle of a refresh that includes brighter lighting, a new ceiling and an updated restroom.
 Passengers who checked luggage should follow the signs to their airline’s designated baggage carousel. Airport employees will also be available to help travelers who need assistance finding their way.
